symptoms: Small dark brown to black spots on leaves, sometimes with yellow halos. Spots may also appear on stems and fruits.
cause: Bacterial infection commonly associated with Xanthomonas species.
treatment: Remove severely infected plant material and use an appropriate copper-based bactericide according to the product label.
prevention: Use disease-free seeds and transplants, avoid overhead watering, improve air circulation, and sanitize gardening tools.

symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings, commonly appearing first on older leaves.
treatment: Remove infected leaves and use an appropriate fungicide according to the product label.
prevention: Rotate crops, avoid overhead watering, improve air circulation, and remove infected plant debris.

symptoms: Large dark water-soaked patches on leaves that can expand rapidly. White fungal-like growth may appear under humid conditions.
treatment: Remove severely infected material and use an appropriate fungicide according to the product label.
prevention: Avoid prolonged leaf wetness, improve air circulation, provide adequate plant spacing, and remove infected debris.

symptoms: Yellowish patches appear on the upper leaf surface while olive-green to brown mold-like growth may develop on the underside.
cause: Fungal infection associated with high humidity and poor air circulation.
treatment: Remove heavily infected leaves and improve ventilation. Use an appropriate fungicide when necessary and follow the product label.
prevention: Reduce humidity, improve air circulation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and provide adequate spacing between plants.

symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and lighter centers, often developing numerous small spots on older leaves.
treatment: Remove infected leaves and use an appropriate fungicide according to the product label.
prevention: Avoid overhead watering, improve air circulation, remove infected plant debris, and maintain good garden sanitation.

symptoms: Fine yellow or pale speckling on leaves, leaf discoloration, drying, and sometimes fine webbing on severely affected plants.
cause: Spider mite infestation, including two-spotted spider mites.
treatment: Remove severely affected leaves and use an appropriate miticide or other approved control method according to the product label.
prevention: Regularly inspect leaves, maintain appropriate plant health, reduce excessive dust, and manage infestations early.

symptoms: Dark circular leaf spots that can develop concentric rings resembling a target. Spots may enlarge and cause leaf damage.
cause: Fungal infection caused by Corynespora cassiicola.
treatment: Remove affected plant material and use an appropriate fungicide according to the product label.
prevention: Avoid overhead watering, improve air circulation, maintain adequate plant spacing, and remove infected debris.

symptoms: Leaves may curl upward, become smaller and yellow, and plant growth may become stunted.
cause: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus, commonly spread by whiteflies.
treatment: Remove severely infected plants where appropriate and manage the insect vector according to local recommendations.
prevention: Control whiteflies, use healthy planting material, remove infected plants, and manage weeds that can harbor vectors.

symptoms: Mottled light and dark green patterns on leaves, distorted foliage, and possible reduction in plant growth.
treatment: Remove infected plants or plant material where appropriate because there is no curative treatment for the virus.
prevention: Use clean tools and healthy planting material, avoid handling plants with contaminated hands, and remove infected plant debris.

symptoms: Leaves appear green and healthy with no obvious disease symptoms or significant pest damage.
treatment: No disease treatment is required. Continue normal plant care.
prevention: Maintain appropriate watering, nutrition, sunlight, air circulation, and regular inspection for pests and diseases.
